data.narrative:
ADASI is a sovereign-funded Defense & Security company that has been acquired. The broader Defense & Security sector contains 24 peers, comprising 2 public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms. Top private comparables include Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, Saronic, and Quantum-Systems.

The peer-median method is not applicable to this valuation. The Defense & Security sector lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage peers meeting comparable criteria; no subsets of three or more datapoints exist within narrow filtering windows (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier). While the broader sector contains 24 players, applying an all-sector median would risk conflating fundamentally different risk, growth, and market-access profiles across heterogeneous development stages and scales.

Given the acquired status and sovereign-funding structure, traditional comparable-company triangulation does not support a reliable valuation range. The absence of sufficient narrow-universe peers—a threshold requirement for median multiples—precludes quantitative synthesis. Further analysis would require either: transaction-level data on the acquisition itself, or expansion of the peer set to adjacent defense-tech verticals with documented financials. The composition of private peers (Anduril, Helsing, Shield AI) suggests the addressable market and typical growth profiles, but without stage-matched, publicly available metrics, no defensible valuation estimate is supportable from this dataset.
